us-west-mountain-p1-laramie-project-temb.summary: The Board of County Commissioners informs residents about a Commercial Site Plan re-submittal and a Conditional Use Permit for a data-center development previously known as Project Jade, now Project Tembo. The earlier submittal, applied for by Crusoe Energy, received governing-body approvals for a zone change to the Switchgrass Industrial Park Planned Unit Development and for the Commercial Site Plan, after public hearings; Tallgrass Energy received matching zone-change and site-plan approvals for the natural-gas Power Hub, whose construction phases are described as well underway. Crusoe has since withdrawn, and the county has discussed the re-submittal with Google (d.b.a. Jupiter Star Holdings, LLC). The revised application reduces the project from five to four buildings (4,025,500 to 3,080,000 sq ft), adds a second permanent entrance on US 85 and halves the peak construction workforce (5,000 to 2,500); because it is smaller than the previously approved Site Plan the county intends to process the Site Plan Revision administratively. A Class B CUP (PZ-26-00057) and commercial site plan for an Office Complex, part of the overall Project Tembo site-plan submittal PZ-26-00058, located directly east of the Switchgrass Industrial Park beside US 85, were to be heard by the Planning Commission on 13 August 2026.
us-west-mountain-p1-laramie-project-temb.title: Laramie County Board of Commissioners memo to residents, 8 July 2026: Project Tembo Data Center Site Plan and Conditional Use Permit

us-west-mountain-p1-prineville-cc-2026-1.summary: Item 7 of the 13 October 2026 council agenda is Resolution 1654 authorizing a development agreement between the City and Apple, Inc. The draft resolution recites that Apple, Inc. owns and operates a data center within Prineville city limits that requires offsite utility infrastructure, and recital A of the attached agreement states that Apple owns and operates a data center campus on real property within the City (Exhibit A). The staff report explains that Apple's initial development plan included expansion of the eastern portion of its campus, which needs offsite utilities: a 16-inch domestic water main, 12-inch non-potable water main, 21-inch sanitary sewer, 12-inch reclaimed/industrial wastewater main, 8-inch gravity and 4-inch pressure sewer lines, bored under Highway 126 in the vicinity of SW High Desert Drive and SW Baldwin Road, serving the eastern portion of the campus, the PRZ 06 development area. The City procures and inspects the work, Apple reimburses up to USD 8,803,435.44 plus an 8.5 percent administrative fee, and the City is to strive for Final Completion by 31 March 2028 and reserve water capacity (99 gpm current plus 350 gpm future). Exhibit A, a Parametrix aerial plan, labels the APPLE CAMPUS north-east of Prineville Airport and east of the SW Connect Way buildings; its flow table assumes 4000 gpm to Apple plus peak demands to Meta and airport industrial users.
